reason: A compound of two existing values, read as a continuum between them like 'linear-lanceolate'. No new term is needed.
'Densely leaved' stems, branches and plants carry well-developed foliage along their axes, which is FLOPO leafy. The degree word 'densely' is dropped, as 'denser' was rejected as a quality before.
The examples mix different missing parts (nectary scales, receptacle paleae, tufts of hair). 'Scale' alone was rejected as a generic part, so the absence has to be stated of the specific part.
Same reading as the earlier rule for 'regular' flowers (C193). Also fits hypanthia and radially symmetrical stems.
A degree adverb split off from its value ('weakly to strongly acuminate'). It is not a quality on its own.
'Rim' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ. The absence can only be stated once the rim is a grounded part (apical rim of an achene, hypanthium rim).
An adverb fragment of ranges such as 'bluntly to acutely conic' or 'bluntly to sharply angled'. The quality is the following value.
Nerveless means without visible veins, the same as the 'veinless' rule (C349). Nerve maps to vascular bundle (C153, C273).
The prefix 'sub-' means approximately, as in 'suborbicular'. The value is PATO terete.
Sheathless bracts and leaves (mainly Carex) lack the basal sheath of the phyllome. PO has a sheath class only for the leaf, so on bracts this rule depends on bract counting as a leaf.
'Perennial grass' names the kind of plant (mostly Poaceae), not a quality of it. The perennial life span is annotated separately.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md: surrounded by (PATO_0005016) towards the enveloping part (e.g. perigynium PO_0009044)
reason: The nutlet or achene is enveloped by another part, usually the perigynium. That is a relation with a second term, and 'loosely' is a degree on it.

label: spine-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's similarity to the appearance of a spine: narrow, rigid and ending in a sharp point. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991200 bract-like and FLOPO:0991143 scale-like; FLOPO:0991210 spine-tipped is a bearer that only ends in a spine.
reason: Hairs, scales, stipules and bracteoles described as spinelike have the whole form of a spine. Neither PATO spiny (covered with spines) nor spine-tipped says this.

Rostellate means having a small beak, the diminutive of rostrate, which is already a synonym of FLOPO beaked. This follows the earlier rule mapping prominulous to the broader prominent. The orchid 'rostelle' example is the part rostellum (FLOPO_0986017), not this quality.
A misspelling and transcription variant ('accre¬scent', 'accrescents') of accrescent, which already exists.
Isophyllous means the leaves of a pair or whorl are alike in size. That is FLOPO equal, said of the leaves. A rule is preferred over a new term; 'anisophyllous' would map to unequal (FLOPO:0991101).

label: gynecandrous
definition: An androgynous quality inhering in an inflorescence by virtue of its pistillate flowers being borne above its staminate flowers on the same axis. NOTE: Child of FLOPO:0991037 androgynous (both staminate and pistillate flowers); a key character of Carex spikes.
reason: A standard Carex character with a fixed meaning. FLOPO androgynous only says both sexes are present and does not give their order.

target: new: coloured marking (punctate PATO_0001512 with the dots red PATO_0000322)
reason: A compound of a marking and its colour, like other 'colour-dotted' and 'colour-spotted' words. One pattern handles all of them better than a term per colour.
Uniserial and French 'unisérié' mean arranged in one row or series, which is FLOPO uniseriate.
A subacaulescent plant has a stem that is present but very short. An approximate absence would wrongly state 'stem absent' in OWL, so the rule is a short stem.

Palmately cleft and 'palmatifide' leaves are lobed with the lobes radiating from one point, so the existing broader term applies (as lobulate maps to lobed). 'Palmatiséqué' (cut to the base) would later need its own palmatisect class.
Dimidiate pinnules and leaflets are developed on one side of the midvein only, an extreme case of the inequilateral shape already mapped to asymmetrical (C236).
Mixes anther dehiscence by pores (already FLOPO:0991153 poricidal) with pores of Sphagnum hyaline cells. 'Pore' was rejected as a generic part.
Lucid leaves and fruits are shining, the same as the 'lustrous' rule (C201). 'Ligid' is a transcription error.
Albuminous seeds have endosperm, and 'albumen' is a synonym of PO endosperm. 'Exalbuminous' would be the matching absence.
Branchlets and rachises ending in a sharp, hardened point. The pointed quality is FLOPO spine-tipped whether the tip is called a thorn or a spine.
Capillaceous means hair-like, very slender, which the 'hair-like' rule already maps to filiform (C317).
Rosettes, seeds and anther locules placed one above another match PATO stacked (same-type entities above and below). The single cotyledon-margin example probably means overlapping and does not fit.
Colliculate seed and fruit surfaces carry small, low, rounded bumps, which falls under FLOPO tuberculate (small rounded protuberances). An existing term is preferred over a finer new one.
A compound of two existing shape values, read as a continuum like 'linear-lanceolate'. No new term is needed.
